newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean clouds clear as Daewoo boss freed.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean clouds clear as Daewoo boss freed.

text.p: The globe-trotting chairman of Daewoo Group on Monday was spared a jail term for bribery that could have rocked the country's third-biggest business concern and cast a shadow over South Korea's shaky economy.
Kim Woo-choong was one of five leading tycoons allowed to walk free by a Seoul appeals court, his two-year sentence suspended for three years.
All five sentences for bribing former president Roh Tae-woo, handed down in August, were either suspended or thrown out.
Jailing several of the biggest names in South Korean business would have sent tremors through a battered economy and a stock market which hit a new three-year low on Monday.

"The market and the general public expected this because the economy is in the pits and the government can't take the chance of depressing it further," said Tae Chung, Jardine Fleming Securities' market strategist in Seoul.
"Foreign bankers wouldn't have been very impressed if they'd had to visit the chairmen of major corporations in jail," said Andrew Holland, BZW Securities' head of research in Seoul.

Daewoo, which recently grabbed world headlines when one of its subsidiaries was jilted by France as a suitor for state-owned Thomson SA's multimedia, would have been hardest hit by the loss of its charismatic chairman.

More so than South Korea's other family-owned conglomerates, or "chaebol", Daewoo is regarded as a one-man show. Kim's hand at the wheel was seen as crucial in guiding the heavily indebted company through a $10 billion overseas expansion drive.
Analysts had long predicted that the tycoons would be granted leniency when the economy, dominated by chaebol, was slowing as a result of falling exports.
The news barely registered on the bourse, as investors worried more about an uncertain economic future, poor market fundamentals, and an oversupply of shares.
The market ended at 673.92, the lowest close since September 4, 1993, when it ended at 665.66.
Lee Kyung-hoon, the chairman of Daewoo Corp, was cleared.
Also acquitted was the chairman of the Hanbo Group, Chung Tae-soo. Jail terms imposed on the chairmen of the Dong-Ah and Jinro groups, Choi Won-suk and Chang Jin-ho, were suspended.

Daewoo Group spokesman Lee Jung-seung said now that the distraction of the trial was behind him, "chairman Kim would make a greater effort to strengthen the group's global strategy and international competitiveness, especially in the automobile sector".
Daewoo is pouring resources into automobiles, with a new plants in Uzbekistan and others planned in the former Eastern Europe.

"We're relieved the sentence was suspended though it was still tough compared to the acquittals of the Daewoo Corp or Hanbo chairmen," said Paik Sang-tae, an official in Dong-ah Construction's PR department.
"In future we will be able to concentrate more on Libyan construction projects and strengthening international competitiveness."
The tycoons were sentenced as part of the "trial of the century", whose star defendants were former presidents Roh and Chun Doo Hwan.
The appeals court commuted Chun's death sentence to life imprisonment and Roh's 22-1/2 year jail term was cut to 17 years.
